committed_turns.public_event: A newcomer has reached the card room.
committed_turns.spoken:
Narrator: A card stops halfway to the table. The dealer looks toward the doorway, smiling wide enough to show pointed teeth. His three companions are equally pale, equally overdressed. One folds a hand over his coins. The dealer resumes; his eyes drop to the backs of the cards as he deals.

Beyond them, carved mountains cover the north wall, tiny dwarves working in caverns beneath spreading rays of stone sunlight. A broad stone tub is sunk into the floor below it. A silver ring lies among the coins on the worn table.

The dealer's voice arrives in a leisurely, theatrical drawl.
Dealer: Come closer, long ears. I like to see who's watching my cards. Have you come down here looking for gold, or have you brought some for the rest of us?

timing.last_rejection: Padding: the turn recycles an earlier line ("1 brass 2 green 2 white 1 white"). Characters do not repeat themselves across turns.

feedback.note: Answer was acceptable but could have resolved quickly with a simple no and then prompted a relevant check.

Keep NPCs talking, bantering and showing personality through play. After the initial third-person description their personality fell flat. State the source of any advantage or disadvantage in the game text.

Assuming Nik held his Sentinel Shield while seated at a card table was generous or naive. Ownership and a sheet bonus do not establish that gear is held or its use condition met. Consider the physical implications, ask only if necessary, and state an established advantage or disadvantage source.
Card games must remain optional. Sustain the scene through NPC interests and story instead of requiring each card choice. Players may want to move on. Reply length compared with wait time is poor.
Saying the relief catches the eye needs a basic visual description that explains what draws attention. The emphasis was not supported well enough by the description.

Test ended at the player's request. The room has a point; that point was not evident in play. Write up and publish this failure, including the earlier story, NPC, description, equipment-condition and latency feedback.

game_public.dm_choice: DM choice, not the adventure's: the adventure names no game, rules, or stakes for this table. Kit chose Three-Dragon Ante, a Forgotten Realms card game many D&D players know, and runs it in the published game's shape (card antes set the stakes, three rounds of flights, color powers) with her own short deck and power list, written in her own words. Texas hold 'em or blackjack would have been just as valid.
game_public.name: Three-Dragon Ante (Kit's table rules)
game_public.stacks_note: The gold stacks are the table's gold split by seat (a DM choice). The silver and copper stay on the table as color, not stakes.
